transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?

Hi Doctor, it's very nice to meet you. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. 

Um... well, I hope I'm explaining this right, but I guess what brings me in is that I just feel like I'm always moving from one thing to the next. I'm just not very good at being idle, which usually isn't a bad thing, right? I've always liked to stay busy. But, um, we recently got a new work setup at my job, and it's just made it a lot harder to... well, to hide it, I guess. 

I don't want to make a mountain out of a molehill, but I figured I should probably come in and talk to someone about it. I hope that's an okay reason to be here?

Would you say this constant need to stay busy and difficulty being idle has been part of who you are since you were a kid, or is this something that's really only become noticeable in the past months or years?

Well, um... I guess if I'm being completely honest, it's probably been there for a long time. Definitely since I was a kid. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just making excuses for myself, but... looking back, it was around long before this recent job change. 

I remember, um, in grade school, my teachers would always write on my report cards that I was a bright kid, which was nice of them to say! But they'd also say I was a bit careless, or that I talked out of turn sometimes. They usually had to remind me to just stay with my work. I was just an energetic kid, you know? I didn't mean any harm by it. Does that make sense? I hope that answers your question.

Besides feeling restless or needing to stay busy, do you often find it hard to sustain your attention on tasks, lose track of details, or get easily distracted when you're trying to focus on something?

Um, yeah, I suppose so. I mean, I try really hard to pay attention, I really do. But, well, sometimes in those longer coaching meetings at work, or if I have to read through a new customer service procedure... I guess I do kind of lose the thread a bit. 

It's not that I don't care about the work! I always start off fine, paying close attention. But then, after a few minutes, I'll realize my eyes have just been moving across the page, or the manager has been talking, and I didn't actually take in anything that was just said. It's a little embarrassing to admit, honestly. I usually just try to catch up on my own later so I don't bother anyone. Is that the kind of thing you mean? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is.
Do you often find yourself interrupting others, blurting out answers, or acting on impulse before thinking things through?

Oh, um... well, I really try my best to be polite, I promise. I don't ever want to step on anyone's toes or seem rude. But, um, sometimes at the call center... if I overhear some of my coworkers trying to figure out a tricky customer problem, I guess I do tend to just jump in. 

I'll just sort of blurt out the solution before they're even done talking, or, well, before anyone actually asked for my help. I just want to be helpful and get the customer taken care of quickly, you know? I really don't mean anything bad by it. I just get so eager to solve the problem that the answer just kind of slips out. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a know-it-all or a bad coworker. Do you think that's normal for someone who just wants to help the team?

Do you often feel physically restless, like you need to get up and move around, or find yourself fidgeting with your hands or feet when you're supposed to stay seated, such as during meetings or long periods at your desk?

Um, well, I guess I do move around a little bit, but I really try to keep it under control so it doesn't bother anyone else. I mean, I know how important it is to be professional, especially when you're older like me and should know better. 

But, um... even when I'm really trying my hardest to sit still and look calm at my desk, I suppose my foot might be bouncing underneath where people can't see it. Or sometimes, I'll realize I've been clicking my pen during a meeting without even noticing I was doing it. I try to stop as soon as I catch myself, though! I'm not trying to be disruptive, I just... I guess my body just wants to do something while I'm sitting there. I hope that's okay to admit. Does that sound like what you're asking about?
Aside from work, do these patterns of restlessness, distractibility, or impulsivity also cause problems for you at home or in your personal relationships?

Oh, um, well... my wife and I have a great relationship, we really do. I certainly don't want to make it sound like we're having big issues or anything. But, I suppose... well, when it comes to the quiet stuff at home? Things that are supposed to relax me, like just sitting down to read, or watching a movie with my wife in the evenings... I guess that can be a little tricky. 

I try my hardest to just settle in and be still with her, I really do. But it usually doesn't last very long before I'm shifting around on the couch, or making comments about the show, or finding an excuse to get up for something, like grabbing a glass of water or checking the thermostat. I always feel a little guilty because I know she just wants a peaceful night, and I don't want to ruin it for her. I just have a hard time doing nothing, I guess. Is that the sort of thing you were looking for? I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad husband, I really do try to let her relax.

Have these patterns of restlessness, distractibility, or impulsivity ever caused real problems for you—like being reprimanded at work, missing important deadlines, or serious friction in your relationships—rather than just feeling like minor annoyances?

Oh, gosh... well, I really hate to admit this, because I always want to be a good employee. And I get along wonderfully with the customers, I really do! But, um... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... it has started showing up just a little bit in my recent performance reviews at work. 

My supervisors—who are very fair, by the way—they've had to point out that I've been leaving some tickets unfinished, or making little mistakes here and there. They mentioned it kind of slows the team down sometimes. I felt just terrible hearing that, because I really am trying so hard, and the last thing I want to do is be a burden to my coworkers. I hope that doesn't make me sound incompetent or like a bad worker. I'm really doing my absolute best to stay on top of things. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
